market: HOU −6, total 40.5. Stroud 32.5 attempts / 21.5 completions; Herbert 31.5 / 18.5 and 4.5 rushes. Woody Marks 16.5 carries; Hampton 10.5.
lineup: HOU RB David Montgomery is out, so Marks is the lead back (Demercado behind him). HOU WR Jaylin Noel and S Reed Blankenship are out. LAC: TE David Njoku out, WR Brenen Thompson and G Kayode Awosika doubtful, and two DBs out. LAC has scored 14.1 points a game.

keys.take: Herbert's legs, the most reliable part of LAC's offense (26 rushing yards a game, 3–5 scrambles most weeks).
keys.how: Rush lanes with contain. HOU forces QBs out of the pocket on 16.4% of dropbacks, the fewest here, and allows 7.9 QB rushing yards a game.
keys.gives: Time to throw, but LAC passes on only 37.5% of neutral downs and its receivers rarely win.
keys.counter: LAC runs its three backs against a run defense allowing 3.91 yards per carry.

keys.take: Nico Collins and C.J. Stroud's intermediate game.
keys.how: LAC's defense is fine (25 points allowed a game, 28 pass attempts against). It tries to shorten the game.
keys.gives: With LAC's offense this weak, the game script.
keys.counter: HOU leads and hands it to Marks.

scripts.control: HOU leads, as expected. LAC has to pass (31.4 attempts a game in its losses), and Herbert's runs depend on pressure that HOU contains rather than collapses.
scripts.competitive: A low-total (40.5) field-position game. Herbert's designed runs are the variable: 0–3 a game this season, with most of his yards on scrambles.
scripts.reversal: LAC leads, Herbert throws less, and HOU throws more. Collins' volume rises.

plays.why: Herbert's rushing comes from scrambles, and HOU is the best defense on the board at keeping QBs in the pocket and holding their runs down.
plays.support: HOU allows 7.9 QB rushing yards and 1.0 scrambles a game, both the lowest here. No QB has run for more than 24 against HOU this season (Allen 24, Lawrence 12, Dak 7, Jones 5).
plays.sample: Herbert went 25+ in 4 of 7 this year. Against this HOU staff he ran for 37 in Week 17 of 2025, and that's the counterexample to weigh.
plays.counter: LAC trailing means more dropbacks, and Herbert is a willing scrambler (5 scrambles in two games this year).
plays.loses: One coverage sack avoided becomes a 20-yard scramble, or LAC calls designed runs to make up for a weak passing game.
plays.vs: Beat under 20 (No 45¢, needs 47%), which leaves no cushion, and under 30 (No 68¢), which is priced past what his 2 of 7 at 30+ supports.
plays.cond: Holds as a final line up to 57¢.
